with_scale.ple_grad_note: PLE gradient not measured: its ~4.7 GB bf16 buffer does not fit one 16 GiB card alongside the full multimodal weights; PLE kept out of the grad target set (exp7 protocol)

scale_stripped.note: base_hidden changes when h0 is unscaled (nonlinearities: attention softmax, tanh-gelu MLP, PLE context projection) — G_out' recomputed on the stripped forward

gemma-4-e2b.decision_rule_result: NOT explained by the embedding gain — structural 'input tyranny' survives scale removal.

part_a.anomaly_note: fp32/CPU run sits in a different numerical regime than bf16/GPU: ||G_in||_fp32 = 5405.7 vs 658.9 (bf16) — an 8x gap too large for dtype rounding; and the sweep breaks first-order linearity, with delta_loss_in flipping sign between eps=1e-4 (-0.337) and eps=1e-3 (+0.087) at magnitudes far below the eps*||G|| predictions (likely tanh softcap 30 saturation dynamics on O(1e2) scaled-embedding hidden states, dtype-sensitive). Part A therefore does NOT confirm functional steepness for this model; the discriminating result is Part B (reproducible: raw ratio 47.14 -> 47.15 across two runs, stripped 5.837 -> 5.841).

interpretation_notes: Part A (epsilon sweep 1e-5..1e-3) is designed to be first-order: Delta-L ~= eps*<G_total,d>, so for a tied matrix its ratio should track the gradient norm ratio. For gemma-4 it did NOT (see part_a.anomaly_note): the fp32/CPU forward is in a different numerical regime than bf16/GPU, so Part A neither confirms nor refutes functional steepness here — the discriminator remains Part B (scale-stripped norms; see decision_rule_result and implied_by_division_only).
Gemma-4 feeds a SECOND scaled embedding table (PLE, scale 16, 2.35B params) into every decoder layer — the input side gets two scaled channels, not one.
